Subject: Post-call: RAG eval recap & recommended next steps

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — really productive. Below is a short recap, our recommended next steps for a focused RAG evaluation, and asks we discussed.

Recap (30-minute scoping call):
- ACME use case: internal knowledge base (policy + product docs) for support agents and sales reps. Medium-sized corpus (~200k docs, mostly PDFs and Confluence pages).
- Primary goals: 1) reduce hallucination / improve grounding; 2) hit 95th pct latency < 200ms for retrieval+generation; 3) maintain token cost targets.
- Constraints: sensitive PII redaction, auditability for compliance team.

Our recommended starting eval plan (short list):
1) Retriever: hybrid BM25+dense (FAISS HNSW) with per-query top_k=100 candidates, then rerank top_k=10.
2) Embeddings: open-sourced text-embedding-3-small baseline for cost; we can A/B with a smaller proprietary embedder if you want stricter grounding.
3) Model(s): Llama-2-13B (4-bit quant) for baseline throughput; for higher precision runs, try RedRun-7B-quant with cross-encoder reranker.
4) Reranker: cross-encoder (pairwise) for final top-10 re-rank — recommended candidate: re-ranker-large-xl. Start with bi-encoder retrieval + cross-encoder rerank to balance recall and precision.
5) Grounding metrics: grounding_score (fraction of tokens with direct doc provenance), exact_match for canonical Q&A, hallucination_rate (manual eval sampled at 200 queries), and precision@k for reranker.

Attachments I’m sending: redwood-rag-eval-results-20270405.csv (sample benchmark), example-prompt-set.md (recommended prompts for eval). Also linking to our RAG eval guide.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Sanjay / Priya: confirm corpus size and whether there is a staging export we can run a smoke eval on (S3 or Drive link).
- Security: you mentioned a short questionnaire — please send or I can share our standard evidence pack.
- Schedule: propose a technical deep-dive with Ethan (solutions engineer) next week to validate retrieval indexing and reranker compute profiles. Please suggest 60-minute slots.

If this looks right I’ll:
- Share an evaluation runbook + test harness (we’ll include the exact prompt set and sampling plan).
- Kick off a smoke eval on a sample export once we have access.

—

Quick technical notes to supplement Marissa’s plan — copying the items Sanjay asked about.

- GPU for re-rank: cross-encoder re-rank at top-10 is usually affordable. Rough rule-of-thumb: re-ranking 1k queries/min with a cross-encoder-large-xl (fp16) needs ~1 A100-style GPU for steady throughput (batching helps). For lower-cost runs we can quantize the reranker and use an RTX-class GPU for sample runs. We’ll provide a detailed compute estimate once we know QPS and SLAs.

- Retrieval config suggestion (practical starting point):
  * index: FAISS HNSW over bi-encoder vectors (dim=1536) + text field for BM25 fallback
  * candidate_k for reranker: 100 -> re-rank top 10
  * scoring: combine dot-product score + BM25 score via a learned linear weight during validation

- Reranker choice: start with a bi-encoder (for recall) + cross-encoder (for precision). If latency/SLOs are tight, we can try a distilled cross-encoder for cheaper CPU/GPU legs.

- Evaluation plan: we’ll run two phases: 1) smoke eval on a 5k-sample from your corpus (random + stratified on doc types); 2) full eval on 50k queries for grounding metrics. For hallucination measurement we’ll use manual annotation of a sampled 200 query set (3 annotators / majority vote).

I’ll attach a short CSV template for the sample run and a link to a Colab that demonstrates re-rank scoring logic.

—
